items.text: $f_*(X')$ represents $Y'\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_E(f^*Y',X')$.
Since $f^*$ turns direct limits into direct limits and $\operatorname{Hom}(-,X')$ turns them into inverse limits, the lemma gives representability.
$f_*$, a right adjoint, commutes with inverse limits; nothing a priori for direct limits. Each of $f^*$, $f_*$ determines the other up to isomorphism.
Definition of a morphism of topoi
A pair of adjoint functors (with adjunction data), $f^*$ left exact:
f=(f^*,f_*),\qquad f^*\dashv f_*,\qquad f^*\ \text{left exact}
« Continuous map » $E\to F$; $f^*$ = inverse image, $f_*$ = direct image.
A category of morphisms
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,F)\quad\text{objects: morphisms of topoi } E\to F
A morphism $f\to g$: either $f^*\to g^*$, or $f_*\to g_*$. Not equivalent choices.
f\mapsto f^*:\ \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,F)\hookrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(F,E)\quad\text{full}
f\mapsto f_*:\ \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,F)\hookrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(E,F)\quad\text{full}
Passing to the adjoint reverses arrows: the two definitions give a category or its opposite.
Take $f_*$ (it goes in the direction of the map), even though $f^*$ carries the exactness.
Difference with spaces: maps do not form a set but a category.
Composition
Associative: topoi form a category.
More: composition is a functor on the Hom categories.
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,F)\times\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(F,G)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(E,G),\quad (f,g)\mapsto gf
(hg)f\simeq h(gf)\qquad(\text{identity here})
Topoi form a 2-category, as categories do: Homs are categories.
A category generalises a set, a 2-category a category...
Spaces (usually) form no 2-category, though one can define it.
Equivalence of topoi
f\colon E\to F\ \text{equivalence}\iff\exists g:\ gf\simeq\mathrm{id}_E,\ fg\simeq\mathrm{id}_F
Equivalent to $f^*$ (or $f_*$) being an equivalence of categories.
Why topoi equivalent as categories are the same geometric object.
Morphisms $\operatorname{Top}(X)\to\operatorname{Top}(Y)$
Isomorphism classes = continuous maps $X\to Y$ ($X$, $Y$ sober). What are the morphisms between $\operatorname{Top}(f)$ and $\operatorname{Top}(g)$?
$X=\mathrm{pt}$: the category of points of $\operatorname{Top}(Y)$ = fibre functors (arrows reversed).
\operatorname{Hom}(\varepsilon_y,\varepsilon_{y'})\neq\varnothing\iff y\in\overline{\{y'\}}
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathrm{pt},Y)\simeq\operatorname{Cat}(Y,\ \text{specialisation order})
General case: at most one morphism $f\to g$, and
\exists\,(f\to g)\iff \forall x\in X:\ g(x)\in\overline{\{f(x)\}}
Product order on $Y^X$, restricted to continuous maps.
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{top}}(\operatorname{Top}X,\operatorname{Top}Y)\ \simeq\ \operatorname{Cat}\bigl(C(X,Y),\le\bigr)\quad\text{rigid}
Hausdorff: discrete orders, hence discrete sets. Non-separated spaces: a hidden 2-category.
